newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia said delaying nuclear power plans.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia said delaying nuclear power plans.

text.p: Indonesia, already rich in energy resources, is revising plans to have a nuclear power plant operational by 2003 and may push it back to 2020 or 2030, the Bisnis Indonesia newspaper reported on Wednesday.

Minister for Research and Technology Jusuf Habibie said the need for a nuclear power plant by 2003 was first identified 20 years ago, before key oil and gas reserves and other energy sources were discovered.

"Maybe we will finally need a nuclear power station in 2020 or 2030. Now we have an excess supply of electricity. Because of that our energy needs need to be revised again," Habibie told a conference in Jakarta.

"This is the result of the finding of natural gas reserves in Natuna, Irian Jaya and Kalimantan as well as the fast development of technology which is supporting efforts in the search for new energy sources," he said.

The Natuna islands, some 1,100 km (689 miles) north of Jakarta in the South China Sea, are home to one of the largest natural gas fields in the world. The remote province of Irian Jaya along with Kalimantan on Borneo island are among the most resource rich areas in Asia.
Last month, Indonesia's parliament passed a controversial nuclear energy bill opposed by anti-nuclear activists who said it did not adequately address safety issues.

Agencies under Habibie's control had previously said they planned to start building a 7,200-megawatt nuclear power station with foreign help at Mount Muria in central Java in 1998 or 1999 pending the results of a feasibility study.
Foreign investors said to have been examining the $7 billion project included Atomic Energy of Canada Ltd, Westinghouse Electric Corp and Mitsubishi Heavy Industries.

State power utility Perusahaan Listrik Negara (PLN), which is to be floated soon, has never included nuclear power in its plans for electricity supply, arguing that it was unecessary in Indonesia which has rich oil, gas and coal reserves.
